summary: Umar scolds Mu'aadh bin Jabal for delaying his departure to jihaad after the army had already left, citing the virtue of one morning or evening in the path of Allaah.

people.name: Abu Zur'ah bin Amr bin Jareer

notes: Narrator has no (RA) marker in the text, so sahabi is unsure.

summary: Ka'b bin Maalik tells how he stayed behind from Tabook without excuse, was boycotted for fifty days, and was forgiven after he chose to speak the truth; the Qur'aan revealed his case.
notes: Abu Qataadah's Companion status is not stated in the text (yes from general knowledge). OCR debris 'Waaqifl' read as Waaqifi.

summary: Abu Imraan reports from Constantinople that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari explained the verse 'do not throw yourselves into destruction' as a warning against staying home to tend fields instead of fighting; a second report repeats the same warning.
notes: Two reports joined. The commander's name in the second report has an OCR gap ('Abdur Rahmaan bin , Khaalid bin Waleed'), so it is not tagged. The Prophet's name is dropped by OCR ('without the knowledge of,'), so mentioned is inferred. Abu Imraan is not linked to approved abu-imraan-jowni (no).

summary: Abu Imraan reports that Abu Ayyoob Ansaari answered those who called a Muhaajir's solo charge self-destruction, explaining that the verse referred to Ansaar who wanted to stay with their families and wealth instead of fighting.
notes: The Prophet's name is dropped by OCR ('in the company of, fought many battles with him'), so mentioned is inferred. Variant of n00563. The Muhaajir is unnamed.

summary: Umar takes land away from Abdullaah bin Harr Anasi after he started farming in Shaam instead of jihaad, and gives it to someone else.

Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas tells Yemeni visitors that the man who takes over a non-Muslim farmer's land in Shaam, with its jizya, and stops jihaad has turned back, not the man who returns to serve his parents.
notes: The Yemeni group is unnamed. Yahya has no (RA) marker, so sahabi is unsure.

summary: Jaabir reports that a quarrel between a Muhaajir and an Ansaari on an expedition was defused by the Prophet, who called their tribal shouting the calls of the Period of Ignorance; Umar offered to kill Abdullaah bin Ubay, which the Prophet refused.
notes: The Prophet's name is dropped by OCR in the 'he exclaimed' and 'said' sentences; read as the Prophet from context.

summary: Urwa bin Zubayr and Amr bin Thaabit report that on the Muraysee expedition the Prophet had Khaalid bin Waleed destroy the idol Manaat; Abdullaah bin Ubay's remark led Umar and Usayd bin Hudhayr to offer to kill him, which the Prophet refused, and Surah Munaafiqoon was revealed.
notes: Bukhari, Muslim, Ahmad, Bayhaqi and Ibn Katheer are references and not tagged. Ibn Is'haaq is named as reporting an addition. OCR debris ignored.

summary: Umar rebukes a man who had guarded the borders for thirty days, asking why he did not complete forty.
notes: Text is cut off after 'Why did you rather not complete forty'. The guard is unnamed.

summary: Umar, patrolling Madinah, hears a woman lamenting her long-absent husband and rules that no army may be kept away from home for more than four months, after consulting his daughter Hafsa; a second chain gives the same account from Abdullaah bin Umar.
notes: Two chains: Ibn Jurayj's (via an unnamed truthful informant) and Abdullaah bin Umar's. The woman and husband are unnamed. Ibn Jurayj has no (RA) marker, so sahabi is unsure.

summary: Rabee bin Zaid reports that the Prophet told a Quraysh youth who avoided walking in the dust that the dust of the path of Allaah is a fragrance from Jannah.
notes: The Quraysh youth is unnamed.

summary: Abul Musabbih reports that Maalik bin Abdullaah Khath'ami urged Jaabir bin Abdullaah to ride; Jaabir replied loudly that he had heard the Prophet say Jahannam is forbidden for feet that become dusty in Allaah's path, and everyone dismounted.
notes: A variant wording attributed to Abu Ya'la is cited within the same narration and is not separately tagged; Abu Ya'la is a reference, not a person in the chain. The Prophet's name is dropped by OCR ('I heard says'), so subject is inferred from the quoted words.

summary: Anas reports that on a journey the fasting Companions collapsed in the heat while those not fasting pitched tents and watered the animals, and the Prophet said those not fasting had taken all the reward.
notes: The speaker's name is dropped by OCR; read as the Prophet from the parallel report in n00574.

summary: A narration cited as Bukhari says the Prophet praised those not fasting on an expedition who served the fasting Companions, giving them all the reward.
notes: Bukhari is a citation and not tagged. Same incident as n00573.

summary: Abu Qilaaba reports that the Companions praised a man who recited the Qur'aan and prayed on every journey, and the Prophet said those who served his travelling needs had gained all his reward.
notes: A second report (Sa'eed bin Jumhaan asking Safeena, a freed slave of the Prophet) is garbled and cut off, so it is not tagged. The Prophet's name is dropped by OCR; read from context.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that during the Battle of Yamaamah, Abdullaah bin Makhrama, lying on the ground and fasting, asked for water to break his fast, but had died before Abdullaah bin Umar returned with it.

Mudrik bin Awf reports Umar's answer to a rumour that his uncle Awf bin Abi Hayya had thrown himself into destruction: Umar said Awf had bought the Aakhirah with this world; Awf kept fasting while wounded until he died.
notes: Mudrik may be the approved 'mudrik' (yes) entry, but the text does not say so, so he is not linked. Awf is also called Abu Shubayl in the text. Neither has a (RA) marker, so sahabi is unsure.

summary: Muhammad bin Hanafiyyah reports that Abu Amr Ansaari, fasting and parched in battle, fired three arrows after recalling the Prophet's saying that an arrow fired in Allaah's path is a light on the Day of Qiyaamah, and was martyred before sunset.
notes: Not linked to approved abu-amr-bin-himaas (unsure); identity not verified. The slave is unnamed.

summary: Ali reports that on the night before Badr every Muslim slept except the Prophet, who prayed under a tree and wept until dawn, and that Miqdaad was the only horseman among them.

Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that at Usfaan the Mushrikeen under Khaalid bin Waleed failed to attack while the Prophet led the Zuhr prayer, and that the Salaatul Khawf verses were revealed between Zuhr and Asr.
notes: Jibra'eel (angel) is named but not tagged. The Mushrikeen are unnamed.

summary: Jaabir reports that the Mushrikeen said a prayer was soon coming that the Muslims loved more than their children.
notes: Variant of n00580. Muslim is a citation and not tagged. The Mushrikeen are unnamed.

summary: Jaabir reports that on the expedition of Dhaatur Riqaa the Prophet appointed Ammaar bin Yaasir and Abbaad bin Bishr to guard the camp; a Mushrik shot Abbaad three times while he prayed, and Abbaad finished his prayer before waking Ammaar.
notes: The Mushrik is unnamed. Abbaad bin Bishr is not linked to the approved 'abbaad' (no) entry, whose identity the list does not establish.

summary: Three items: Abbaad bin Bishr keeps praying while Ammaar sleeps; Heraclius asks why the Romans are being defeated and is told the Muslims pray at night and fast by day; and Hind tells Abu Sufyaan that the night worship in the Masjid was unlike anything she had seen.
notes: Three items joined. The Abu Is'haaq citation and the cross-reference to an earlier chapter are not tagged as people. Editorial sentences ('More Ahadeeth ... will be discussed') are ignored. The Prophet is mentioned only as the object of Hind's pledge.

summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that after the conquest of Makkah the Muslims recited takbeer and tahleel and made tawaaf until dawn; the Prophet repeated to Abu Sufyaan what he had said privately to Hind, and Abu Sufyaan testified to his prophethood.
notes: The text writes 'Musayyib'; the approved entry is 'Sa'eed bin Musayyab' (no). The text marks him (RA), which the approved list does not; the approved id is used.

summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports that on the way to Khaybar the Prophet stopped the Companions from shouting takbeer in a valley, and taught him 'there is no power or might except with Allaah' as a treasure of Jannah.
notes: The text addresses the narrator as 'Abdullaah bin Qais', which is his own name, so no second person is tagged.

summary: Jaabir reports that the Companions on the journey said takbeer when climbing an incline and tasbeeh when descending.
notes: No approved dhikr theme exists, so duaa is used as the nearest approved id and dhikr is proposed as new.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar describes two kinds of people on an expedition: those who stay conscious of Allaah and spend generously, and those who lack dhikr, avoid the fighting, boast, and misappropriate the booty, and so have no share of the reward.
notes: A statement attributed to Abdullaah bin Umar; the Prophet is not mentioned.

summary: Section heading only: 'Making Du'aa when leaving a place', with no narration.
notes: Heading text only; there is no report in this entry.

summary: Ibn Is'haaq reports the du'aa the Prophet made when leaving Makkah for Madinah, asking Allaah for protection, companionship and steadfastness.
notes: Ibn Is'haaq says he was informed of this and names no source, so the chain is not tagged further.

summary: The grandfather of Abu Marwaan Aslami reports the du'aa the Prophet made on seeing Khaybar, asking for the good of the town and protection from its evil, then ordering the Companions to advance in Allaah's name.
notes: The narrator is unnamed. Abu Marwaan Aslami appears only as the narrator's grandson and is not tagged.

summary: A narration cited as Tabraani says the Prophet made this same du'aa each time he entered a town.
notes: Tabraani is a citation and not tagged. The jihaad theme comes from the heading, as the du'aa belongs to the expedition chapter.

summary: Umar reports that at Badr the Prophet, facing many more enemies, prayed towards the Qiblah until his upper garment fell off; Abu Bakr put it back and reminded him of Allaah's promise, and Surah Anfaal 9 was revealed.
Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas reports the Prophet's du'aa at Badr for his 315 Companions' transport, clothing and food, and that after victory each of them had one or two camels and ate their fill.

Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that the Prophet's du'aa at Badr, pleading on Allaah's promise, was the most persistent he had heard, and that the Prophet then said he could see where the dead Mushrikeen would fall by nightfall.

Two reports: Anas says the Prophet repeatedly prayed for help at Uhud, and Abu Sa'eed Khudri says that at the Battle of the Trench the Prophet taught the Companions a du'aa after which Allaah sent a powerful wind against the enemy.
notes: Two reports joined (Uhud, then Khandaq). The Companions who asked are unnamed.

summary: Jaabir reports that at Masjid Ahzaab the Prophet stood and cursed the Mushrikeen without prayer the first time, then cursed them again and prayed two rakaahs.
notes: Masjid Ahzaab is a place name. The Mushrikeen are unnamed.

summary: Three narrations: the Prophet cursed the confederate forces attacking Madinah, asking Allaah to defeat and shake them; another du'aa asks for victory; and Abu Hurayrah relates a du'aa praising Allaah as the one who alone defeated the coalition.
notes: Bukhari and Muslim are citations and not tagged. Abu Hurayrah is named as narrator of the third item only.

summary: Ali reports that during Badr he went to check on the Prophet, who was in sajdah repeatedly saying 'Yaa Hayyu, Yaa Qayyoom' and kept doing so until Allaah granted victory.
notes: Trailing heading text ('Making Du'aa During the night...') is OCR debris and is ignored.

summary: Ali reports that on the night before Badr the Prophet prayed through the night for the destruction of that group, and that rain fell, making the ground firm for the Muslims and muddy for the enemy.
Ali reports that although the Prophet was a traveller, he spent the whole night before Badr in worship until morning.
notes: Another report from Ali, closely related to n00579.
